item.title: U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history
item.description: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law, fueling a backlash that critics say is as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.
item.content:encoded: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law, fueling a backlash that critics say is as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.

item.title: Inside a Chicago home, a photographer documents the life her family built
item.description: For eight years, photographer Jennifer Teresa Villanueva has documented her Mexican American family's everyday life in Chicago, capturing intimate moments of love, labor and sacrifice.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back
item.description: The Trump administration provided few details about its process for canceling hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollments — even as the next stage of the anti-fraud effort is underway.

item.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries, officials say, after brief truce
item.description: Ukrainian drones attacked a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region early Thursday, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over.

item.title: Trump cancels public execution, but a line may already have been crossed
item.description: Defense Secretary Hegseth's announcement of a livestreamed execution elicited reactions of disgust and condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. But within his church, it's not an outlier.

item.title: School roof collapse kills at least 29, injures more than 3 dozen in Pakistan
item.description: The roof of a private school collapsed in northwestern Pakistan on Thursday, killing at least 28 children and a female teacher and injuring more than 50 other people.
